'''Idit Zehavi''' ({{langx|he|עדית זהבי}}; born 1969) is an Israeli [[astrophysicist]] and researcher who discovered an anomaly in the mapping of the cosmos, which offered insight into how the universe is expanding. She is part of the team completing the [[Sloan Digital Sky Survey]] and is one of the world's most highly cited scientists according to the list published annually by Thomson [[Reuters]].

== Biography ==
Idit Zehavi was born in Israel in 1969<ref name="hired  and birth">{{cite news|title=Brain Gain: Idit Zehavi|url=http://www.cleveland.com/businessmonday/wide/index.ssf?/businessmonday/wide/11braingain27.html|access-date=20 November 2015|publisher=[[The Plain Dealer]]|date=27 November 2006|location=Cleveland, Ohio|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151121045153/http://www.cleveland.com/businessmonday/wide/index.ssf?%2Fbusinessmonday%2Fwide%2F11braingain27.html|archive-date=21 November 2015}}</ref> and completed her education in [[Jerusalem]], earning a [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] from the [[The Racah Institute of Physics|Racah Institute of Physics]] at the [[Hebrew University of Jerusalem]] in 1998.<ref name="The Hebrew University of Jerusalem">{{cite web|title=Cosmology Group|url=http://www.phys.huji.ac.il/~dekel/group.html|publisher=The Hebrew University of Jerusalem|access-date=20 November 2015|location=Jerusalem, Israel}}</ref> That same year, while researching the expansion of the universe, she and a senior colleague, [[Avishai Dekel]], noted an anomaly in the cosmos which suggested that the portion of the galaxy where earth lies  is expanding faster than the entirety of the universe. The findings were independently noted by another researcher, [[Adam Riess]], from the [[University of California, Berkeley]].<ref name=expansion>{{cite news|title=Supernovas Light Up Cosmic Growth Spurt|url=https://www.science.org/content/article/supernovas-light-cosmic-growth-spurt|access-date=20 November 2015|publisher=Science Magazine|date=15 May 1998|location=American Association for the Advancement of Science}}</ref> Soon after, Zehavi moved to the United States to complete her post-doctorate studies in [[galaxy clustering]] at the [[University of Chicago]] and participate in research at the [[Fermi National Accelerator Laboratory]].<ref name=FermiNews>{{cite journal|last1=Perricone|first1=Mike|title=Friends of Friends|journal=FermiNews|date=21 March 2003|volume=26|issue=5|url=https://www.fnal.gov/pub/ferminews/ferminews03-03-21/p1.html|access-date=20 November 2015|publisher=[[Fermilab]]|location=Batavia, Illinois}}</ref> She left Fermilab in 2004 for the [[University of Arizona]] and continued working on the research of the [[Sloan Digital Sky Survey]] (SDSS).<ref name="Sloan Sky Survey">{{cite news|title=Astronomers Find Gravity's Signature in Galaxy Distribution|url=http://uanews.org/story/astronomers-find-gravity-s-signature-in-galaxy-distribution|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151121024203/http://uanews.org/story/astronomers-find-gravity-s-signature-in-galaxy-distribution|url-status=usurped|archive-date=November 21, 2015|access-date=20 November 2015|publisher=UA News|date=14 January 2005|location=University of Arizona, Tucson, Arizona}}</ref> In 2005, she participated in research under the direction of Daniel Eisenstein, which detected "cosmic ripples",<ref name=ripples>{{cite news|title=SDSS Measures Size of the Universe; Finds Big Bang Echo in Galaxy Distribution|url=http://www.fnal.gov/pub/today/archive/archive_2005/today05-04-07.html|access-date=20 November 2015|publisher=Fermilab Today|date=7 April 2005|location=Batavia, Illinois}}</ref> which confirmed the cosmological theory of the creation of the universe.<ref name="big bang confirmed">{{cite journal|title=Detection of the Baryon Acoustic Peak in the Large-Scale Correlation Function of SDSS Luminous Red Galaxies|arxiv=astro-ph/0501171|date=10 Jan 2005|author1=D. J. Eisenstein |author2=I. Zehavi |author3=D. W. Hogg |author4=R. Scoccimarro |author5=M. R. Blanton |author6=R. C. Nichol |author7=R. Scranton |author8=H. Seo |author9=M. Tegmark |author10=Z. Yanny |author48=D. York |doi=10.1086/466512 |volume=633 |journal=The Astrophysical Journal |issue=2|pages=560–574 |bibcode=2005ApJ...633..560E|s2cid=4834543}}</ref>

In 2006, she joined [[Case Western Reserve University]] of [[Cleveland, Ohio]], as an Associate Professor in the Astronomy Department.<ref name="hired  and birth" /><ref name=professor>{{cite web|title=Idit Zehavi|url=https://artsci.case.edu/faculty/idit-zehavi/|publisher=[[Case Western Reserve University]]|access-date=20 November 2015|location=Cleveland, Ohio}}</ref> In 2009, Zehavi was awarded a grant from the U.S. [[National Science Foundation]] to continue her work with the SDSS to expand her work on galaxy clustering to encompass a larger scale view of the universe.<ref name="National Science Foudation">{{cite web|title=From Galaxy Clustering to Galaxy Formation and Evolution|url=http://grantome.com/grant/NSF/AST-0907947|publisher=Grantome|access-date=20 November 2015 |last1=Zehavi |first1=Idit |last2=Zheng |first2=Zheng }}</ref> According to the annual listing produced by Thomson [[Reuters]], Zehavi is one of the world's most highly cited scientists.<ref name="highy cited">{{cite web|title=The World's Most Influential Scientific Minds|url=http://sites.biology.duke.edu/donglab/images/papers/thomas_reuter_2014.pdf|publisher=[[Thomson Reuters]]|access-date=20 November 2015|date=2014|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151117020628/http://sites.biology.duke.edu/donglab/images/papers/thomas_reuter_2014.pdf|archive-date=17 November 2015}}</ref>
